transport: Bluetooth only. No VE.Direct port, no CAN, no wired data connection — two wires to the battery for power and voltage sense, and a built-in temperature sensor.
gotchas: No documented protocol at all in any committed source, and this is the cleanest negative result in the set. The committed BLE specification's record-type table runs 0x00 Test, 0x01 Solar Charger, 0x02 Battery Monitor, 0x03 Inverter, 0x04 DC/DC, 0x05 SmartLithium, 0x06 Inverter RS, 0x07 GX-Device (TBD), 0x08 AC Charger

What it actually does is feed battery voltage and temperature to a Victron charger over VE.Smart networking — Victron's proprietary Bluetooth mesh between its own products. docs/catalog/ve-direct.md already records the receiving end of that: MPPT HEX register 0xEDEC battery temperature is populated "only from firmware
That indirection is the practical answer and it costs nothing: a cabin that already has a Victron MPPT on VE.Direct gets battery temperature through a register it is already reading.

It is a `environment-sensor`/`battery`-adjacent device by function but reports through another device's map, which the catalogue's dialect model does not have a shape for. Worth noting when the format is next revised.
checked: 2026-07-31 — 2 Quebec retailers, which puts it above most of this file on ownership probability and at the bottom on protocol tractability.
